name: pnp-sharepoint-skills-interactive-3d-scene
title: Interactive 3D Scene
shortDescription: Builds a self-contained, clickable 3D scene as one HTML file for the SharePoint HTML viewer. The file holds the scene and its assets, requests Babylon.js with the host manifest, and uses a flat SVG fallback when 3D is unavailable.
longDescription: Turns a theme or occasion, such as a team celebration, a seasonal greeting or a product launch, into a playful 3D scene with 3 to 6 tappable objects that glow, bounce, shake, spin, flash or burst into sparks.

Outputs a single self-contained HTML file that follows the SharePoint HTML viewer rules. Self-contained means the scene, script, styles and drawn assets are in the file. Babylon.js is requested through the host ka-lib-manifest. When window.BABYLON is available and WebGL works, the page is true 3D and the camera can orbit within the scene's limits. A finished SVG drawing with the same click and tap reactions is the fallback when the library or WebGL is unavailable, and when mode=2d is set.

Includes keyboard and button access, a live status line, reduced motion support, sound synthesized with Web Audio that stays off until the viewer turns it on, and a demo mode for 16:9 or 9:16 screen recordings. Ships with a starter template and reference guides so the pattern can be reused for any theme. On 6 November 2026, I tested the original HTML scenes in SharePoint with Babylon.js loaded through ka-lib-manifest. They rendered in true 3D, with camera pan and orbit, without bundling the library into the HTML file. The starter and sample files keep a limited orbit with target panning disabled; that is a scene choice, not a SharePoint restriction.
